source_text: Verum quia id impendio poposcisti, immo indixisti auctoritate patria, ut libro tractatoris Poeni, quem ad Valerium comitem vernula peccatorum eius Alypius nuper detulit, obviarem, hinc mihi est longior facta responsio.
pass_a_gloss: But because you asked it urgently, nay imposed it by a father's authority, that I should meet the book of the Punic expositor, which Alypius, the little house-slave of his sins, recently carried to Count Valerius, from this my answer has been made longer.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS Poenus=Carthaginian; Julian's slur for Augustine

pass_b_english: But you urgently requested, or rather ordered with a father's authority, that I answer the African expositor's book, which Alypius, the household slave of his sins, recently carried to Count Valerius. That is why my reply has grown longer.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's ethnic-rhetorical slur for Augustine; keep the geographic sting rather than neutralizing it.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
